name: SFPUC Customer Assistance Program (CAP) - water and sewer discount
agency: San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)
who: One SFPUC water and sewer account in your name; full-time residence at the address; individually metered residential single-family account (not fire service, multi-unit residential, irrigation, commercial or wholesale); not claimed as a dependent on someone else's tax return. 2026 combined gross household income limits: 40% discount tier $34,050 (1 person), $38,900 (2), $43,750 (3), $48,650 (4); 25% discount tier $56,750 (1), $64,850 (2), $72,950 (3), $81,050 (4).
benefit: 25% or 40% off the SFPUC water and sewer bill. Discount lasts 36 months, then you must reapply. CAP enrollees are exempt from water shutoffs and liens.
apply_where: Online application linked from the CAP page (income verified through TransUnion), or print and mail the paper form, or pick up at the SFPUC Customer Service Counter, 525 Golden Gate Ave, 1st Floor, San Francisco. Applicants already receiving SF Human Services Agency benefits can authorize income verification on the paper form. If denied, you must wait three months before a new paper application.
apply_phone: (415) 551-3000 (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm, except holidays; request mailed paper application)
form: CAP application (online form, or printable PDF)
auto_via: SF Human Services Agency benefits can be used to verify income
status_2026: Active. 2026 income limits are published on the SFPUC page. Processing takes 3-4 weeks.

name: EBMUD Customer Assistance Program (CAP) - water and wastewater discount
city: Oakland (East Bay Municipal Utility District service area)
agency: East Bay Municipal Utility District (EBMUD)
who: Household meets CAP income guidelines (single-family residents: $67,900 or less for 1-2 persons, $76,400 for 3, $84,850 for 4, $91,650 for 5, $98,450 for 6, plus $6,800 per additional person) (U - income table on page has no year label; confirm current year). Bill in your name; residential account with an individual water meter; not claimed as a dependent on someone else's tax return; one account per household.
benefit: 50% off the standard bimonthly service charge; 50% off home water use up to 1,050 gallons per person per month; 35% off wastewater service and flow charges. Enrollment lasts up to two years (you are notified two months before expiration). Not retroactive.
apply_where: Apply online at ebmud.com/cap (confirmation email includes an Application/Confirmation ID; reply to that email with documents, per EBMUD instructions). Or download the form and mail, email (cap@ebmud.com), or fax (510) 287-0299. Pick up in person at EBMUD Customer Information Desk, 375 11th St., Oakland, ground floor.
apply_phone: 866-403-2683 (U - listed in a search summary of the EBMUD page; confirm)
status_2026: Active. Program page lists the income table without a year label (U).

name: San Jose Water Customer Assistance Program (CAP) - water bill discount
city: San Jose (and other San Jose Water service areas)
agency: San Jose Water (investor-owned utility, regulated by the CPUC)
who: Bill in your name (or submetered mobile-home tenant); household gross income from all sources at or under the June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027 limits: $43,280 (1-2 persons), $54,640 (3), $66,000 (4), $77,360 (5), $88,720 (6), $100,080 (7), $111,440 (8), plus $11,360 per additional person (from tariff Schedule CAP AL626, June 2026). Not claimed as a dependent. Enrollment in PG&E CARE or a CPUC-authorized income declaration is required; declaration renews every two years.
benefit: 15% discount on the total water bill.
apply_where: Apply through sjwater.com (CAP page). Reapply when you move; notify San Jose Water within 30 days if you become ineligible.
form: CPUC-authorized income eligibility declaration (U - form not retrieved)
auto_via: PG&E CARE enrollment (satisfies the declaration requirement per the tariff)
status_2026: Active. Tariff effective June 1, 2026.

name: LA Metro LIFE (Low Income Fare is Easy)
city: Los Angeles County (valid on Metro and 16 participating agencies, including Long Beach Transit)
agency: LA County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro)
who: Age 18 or older and head of household. Income limits (U - from a secondary source; official page lists them without a year): $58,300 (1 person), $66,650 (2), $74,950 (3), $83,300 (4), plus $6,650 per additional person. Or enrolled in CalFresh/EBT/SNAP, Medi-Cal, SSI, General Relief or other public assistance. Photo ID for each applicant listed; LA County residency needed.
benefit: First 90 days: free unlimited rides on Metro and participating agencies. After that choose 20 free rides per month (rides roll over) or discounted passes (up to $24 off a monthly pass or EZ Pass). Reduced Fare TAP discounts can be combined. South LA and Pomona ZIP codes get 6 extra months of free rides.
apply_where: Apply online at taptogo.net (LIFE application, under 10 minutes). Paper applications and in-person help at Metro Customer Centers, community events, or International Institute of Los Angeles offices (Southwest LA 323-870-8567; Northwest Van Nuys 818-527-4464; Southeast El Monte 818-244-2550).
form: Online LIFE application; paper application available by email lifeinfo@metro.net
auto_via: Social Security or SSDI (U - from a secondary source)
status_2026: Active per Metro page (U on whether 2026 income table is current).

name: Clipper START (Bay Area income-based discount) and SF Muni Lifeline Pass
city: San Francisco and the 9-county Bay Area
agency: Bay Area transit agencies via MTC Clipper program; SFMTA for Muni Lifeline Pass
who: Household adjusted gross income at or under 200% of federal poverty level. 2026 limits per SFMTA page: $31,920 (1 person), $43,280 (2), $66,000 (4); $11,360 more per person beyond the table (U - the 3-person figure is printed with a typo on the page; confirm). Live in the Bay Area (U). Age rules in older materials (ages 19-64) are unverified for 2026.
benefit: Muni Lifeline monthly pass at $43 (50% off a regular Muni monthly pass) for the full calendar month; Clipper START also offers single-ride discounts.
apply_where: Apply at clipperstartcard.com; provide proof of identity and income. CalFresh recipients can sign in with Login.gov. Medi-Cal, EBT or WIC card copies can be used as proof. Otherwise complete the Income Verification Form. SFMTA Customer Service Center: 11 South Van Ness Ave, San Francisco.
form: Clipper START online application; Income Verification Form (paper)
status_2026: Active per SFMTA 2026 page. SFMTA says the Lifeline pass is moving to Clipper START (timing unclear, U).

name: Free Muni for youth (under 19)
agency: SFMTA
who: Youth under 19 (U - an SFMTA podcast page says 18 and younger; a climate profile says under 19). Ages 19-22 who are English learners or in special education (U). No income or residency test per 2021 SFMTA announcement.
benefit: Free rides on Muni buses, streetcars and metro trains. Cable cars not covered for non-residents (per 2021 notice).
apply_where: No application as of 2021 announcement. Check SFMTA for current rules.
apply_web: SFMTA Young People Ride Muni Free
status_2026: Unverified (U). Last confirmed funding was through FY2024; no 2026 notice found.

name: Youth Opportunity Pass (free transit for youth)
agency: San Diego MTS and SANDAG (Youth PRONTO)
who: Youth 18 and under (MTS page says ages 6-18 with a Youth PRONTO card or app account; U). Children 5 and under ride free without a card. Proof of age required (school ID, birth certificate or government photo ID).
benefit: Free rides on MTS and NCTD. Pass valid until 19th birthday (U).
apply_where: Create a Youth PRONTO app account or get a Youth PRONTO card; send proof of age.
apply_web: MTS Youth Ride Free with PRONTO
form: Youth PRONTO account or card; proof-of-age upload
status_2026: Active. Hoodline (June 2026) reports SANDAG extended it through June 2027 (U). Older MTS pages still show June 30, 2026 end date.

name: Tenant Right to Counsel (TRC) - free eviction defense
agency: City and County of San Francisco (funded through the Eviction Defense Collaborative and partner nonprofits)
who: Tenants facing an eviction notice or unlawful detainer complaint in San Francisco. Not limited by income in the admin code provision (U).
benefit: Free attorney representation or litigation help in an eviction case. Coverage starts 30 days after the eviction notice, or at service of the complaint, whichever is first. Program reports 93% success rate (advocate figures).
apply_where: Contact the Eviction Defense Collaborative or your tenant rights group; apply through the TRC intake process.
status_2026: Active. A TRC Coordinator job posting shows the program operating with July 1, 2026 start (U).

name: Stay Housed LA (eviction defense and short-term rental assistance)
agency: Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) and LA County (joint program); Legal Aid Foundation of Los Angeles is the main legal provider
who: Low-income tenants facing an unlawful detainer case. Rental assistance is reserved for income-eligible households (U - exact income limit not verified).
benefit: Free limited or full-scope legal representation in eviction cases; short-term rental assistance to settle or prevent eviction; other supportive services.
apply_where: Contact Stay Housed LA intake through LAHD or the Legal Aid Foundation of Los Angeles.
status_2026: Active. LA City Council approved LAHD contracts in March 2026 for a 15-month initial funding period (U).

name: Keep Oakland Housed
agency: City of Oakland with nonprofit partners (Bay Area Community Services, Catholic Charities of the East Bay, East Bay Community Law Center)
who: Households at or below 50% of area median income facing eviction or homelessness (U - from older program materials).
benefit: Eviction legal representation and up to $7,000 in rent or financial help paid to landlord or vendor.
apply_where: Call 211 or contact a partner agency.
status_2026: Unverified (U). No 2026 source found confirming it is operating.
